title: Nasruddin Tale 179: The Olive Tree
summary: An eighty-year-old Nasruddin was planting a tiny olive shoot that would take forty years to bear fruit....
full_text:
An eighty-year-old Nasruddin was planting a tiny olive shoot that would take forty years to bear fruit.

A young man scoffed: "Mulla, you will never live to taste the olives of that tree!"

Nasruddin patted the earth: "Our grandfathers planted olive trees whose fruit we enjoy today; we plant today so our grandchildren may eat tomorrow. Life is a chain of giving, not a banquet for one!"
moral: We plant trees not for ourselves alone, but so future generations may harvest peace.
